item.title: Economic Development Committee Discusses Prioritizing Public Engagement
item.description: Newton’s Economic Development Committee met Tuesday to discuss ways to manage and increase public engagement in their work, citing a public committee newsletter and teen community spaces as ideas for boosting community involvement in the committee.

item.title: Land Use Committee Amends Wells Avenue Deed Restriction for Veterinary Hospital Addition
item.description: On Tuesday evening, Newton’s Land Use Committee unanimously approved the request to amend the Wells Avenue Deed Restriction for 60 Wells Ave., permitting the addition of a veterinary hospital.

item.title: Brian Davids Wins 2026 Martin Luther King Jr. Scholarship
item.description: Cheers erupted, and a standing ovation ensued in the Heights Room on Wednesday night as Brian Davids was named the 2026 Martin Luther King, Jr. Scholarship winner.

item.title: ‘Wicked’ Star Marissa Bode Discusses the Importance of Disability Visibility in the Arts
item.description: Bode, who portrayed Nessarose in Wicked and Wicked: For Good—and was the first actress with a disability to take on the role—imparted wise insights regarding the importance of representation and visibility in Hollywood, as well as in everyday life.

item.title: ChatGPT Has a Place on Your Playlist, and You Don’t Even Know It
item.description: The question of AI’s place in music is just one moral dilemma out of the myriad that have surfaced since ChatGPT’s genesis in early 2023. Over the last three years, computer science college dropouts, following in the footsteps of OpenAI founder Sam Altman, have flooded the web with what’s estimated to be hundreds of thousands of large language models (LLMs).

item.title: No Luck Needed: What To Know About Boston’s St. Patrick’s Day Parade
item.description: The South Boston St. Patrick’s Day Parade is one of Boston’s most treasured traditions. Here’s what you need to know to enjoy the festivities this Sunday, March 15.

item.title: Preview: No. 4-Seeded BC Hosts No. 5-Seeded Maine in Hockey East Quarterfinals
item.description: After finishing out its regular season with four straight losses, No. 4-seeded Boston College men's hockey will begin the Hockey East Tournament by hosting No. 5-seeded Maine in what has become a do-or-die stretch for the Eagles' postseason chances.

item.title: From Fitz Bathroom to Basement Barbershop: The Rise of Club Kirk Cuts
item.description: “It started as ‘fake till you make it,’” Olohan said. “But now when someone sits in the chair, I’m confident we’re not going to have any issues.”

item.title: Two Teams Announce Bids for UGBC President, Vice President
item.description: Two teams announced bids for UGBC president and vice president Thursday morning, unveiling their campaigns through Instagram posts on their respective profiles.
